thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for /v1/stream (eu-west-2). p99 > 3.2s for last 5m, error-rate climb 0.6% :rotating_light:
Dana: acked, oncall here. seeing streaming stalls reported by users.
Mike: I’m looking at metrics now — p95 up ~600ms, p99 up to 3s+, tail stalls where TLS handshake time shoots up.
Sasha: adding logs — connection handshake times jump around 250–1200ms. TLS handshake count spikes correlate with cross-AZ NAT egress.
Dana: any network events in infra? crosszone routing?
Henry: Cloud console shows NAT gateway SNAT port exhaustion alarm around 17:23 UTC for a subset of VPCs in eu-west-2a/2c. ephemeral port usage at ~96%.
Irene: Confirmed. conntrack table growth + NAT ports approaching limits on nat-01-eu-west-2a.
oncall: paging rotation noted — @Dana will lead triage. Mike you own mitigations, Sasha owns logs/tracing, Henry own infra changes.
Dana: quick customer impact check — which customers hit?
Sasha: Correlating request IDs — streaming sessions that created >50 concurrent outbound connections show increased resets. Looks like a handful of high-concurrency customers and internal load tests.
Mike: immediate mitigation plan: 1) scale out NAT (add 2x nat gateways / additional EIPs) 2) transit traffic for streaming pool via alternate egress subnet with spare NATs 3) apply short-term TCP keepalive to reuse connections (where possible)
Henry: spinning up additional NATs, allocating EIPs. ETA ~4m.
Dana: we should also route non-critical tenant traffic to an alternate region? Risky. Prefer local egress scaling first.
Irene: I can flip routing policy for the streaming worker ASG to prefer subnet-b with spare NATs (controlled failover). Doing a staged route change to avoid routing loops.
Sasha: posting relevant traces: <https://grafana.internal/streams/d/abcd|streaming-handshake-panel> — you can see TLS timeouts aligned with NAT port saturation.
Mike: small mitigation: enable connection pooling proxy on streaming frontends to reuse upstream and reduce outbound connection churn. Config change roll underway (non-disruptive).
Dana: also enable TLS session resumption hints in edge config so clients can resume. That reduces full-handshake rate.
incident-bot: NOTE: Incident severity updated to Sev2. Paging to SRE.
Henry: NATs provisioned and attached. Starting drain/rehoming of routes now.
Sasha: logs show immediate drop in new handshake durations after NAT scale begins — looks promising.
Mike: rolling config applied to frontends (conn pool + keepalive). Monitoring shows p95 down to ~220ms, p99 trending toward 900ms.
Dana: customer impact: SLOs were breached for p99 for ~18m window during spike. Affected customers: 5 customers (IDs masked) with active streaming sessions; no data loss reported, but some session resets and reconnections.
Irene: doing a quick audit: no packet loss at VPC level, but retransmit counts rose on crosszone links consistent with transient NAT queueing.
Sasha: recording an example request trace for the postmortem: session start -> 302ms TLS -> 1.6s handshake spike -> reconnect.
Mike: current mitigation status: NAT pool expanded, routing adjusted, frontends conn-pool live. Traffic normalized.
Dana: open actions: 1) increase default SNAT port pool or add ephemeral IPs to NAT fleet, 2) implement per-tenant egress limits and connection pooling in SDKs, 3) add alert for NAT port saturation earlier (80% threshold), 4) run chaos test for NAT exhaustion during canary.
Irene: I'll create infra PR to make additional NATs autoscaled and add 80% alert.
Henry: we should also consider using proxy egress (shared long-lived connections) for worker pools. Will prototype next week.
Sasha: will file a tracing/regression alert so we get early signal when handshake durations spike beyond baseline.
Dana: customer comms — ops will draft a short note summarizing impact and remediation; we hit SLO window breach for 18m, mitigation applied. Mike you draft.
Mike: will draft and send for review within 1h.
incident-bot: RESOLVED: p99 latency returned below threshold for 10m. Auto-close check at +30m.
Dana: leaving incident open for postmortem and action items. Handing over to follow-up owners: Irene (infra), Sasha (observability), Mike (customer comms).
Henry: note for postmortem: a recent deployment to streaming workers increased per-process concurrency — likely root contributor to port exhaustion.
Sasha: dumping logs and traces to the incident folder: gs://redwood-incidents/1836123456/
Irene: creating infra-ticket: INFRA-2478 "Autoscale NAT fleet & add 80% SNAT alert"
Mike: customer comm note draft: "We experienced elevated streaming latency for ~18 minutes in eu-west-2 due to transient NAT egress saturation leading to increased TLS handshake latency. We scaled NAT capacity and applied connection pooling which restored normal service. No data loss; some sessions were reset and reconnected. Follow-up: autoscale NAT, SDK pooling, and improved alerts."
Dana: thanks team. We'll run a blameless postmortem tomorrow 10:00 UTC. Please attach all logs/PRs to the incident doc. :thumbsup:
Irene: leaving an action item link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/INFRA-2478
Sasha: adding a note to monitoring runbook to check ephemeral ports and conntrack during cross-AZ peaks.
Mike: closing oncall shift for this incident, handing to follow-up owners.
Dana: incident channel keep open for 2h for any regressions. If p99 > 1s spike again, re-pager.
incident-bot: Incident timeline saved to gs://redwood-incidents/1836123456/timeline.json
